scope: Documented independent Java/Spring and MySQL/MariaDB workflows on Windows; no claim of complete IntelliJ IDEA or DataGrip parity.
nodeEvidenceScope: Both complete actual Spring/database Node suites retain their original MF402 execution receipts and verified freshness. Their product payloads, Node test definitions, reachable workspace dependencies, fixture definitions and launch-wrapper source bytes match the final release. Three later source deltas affect only test/java-move-v21-host.js (one exact expected-error assertion) and test/java-change-signature-v20-host.js plus test/java-change-signature-v21-host.js (reviewed owned-document pinning, native baseline revert and editor focus). All three native helpers are outside the audited Node dependency closure; fresh unit, public reproduction and native checks use the final source vector.

nativeFixturePrecondition.description: Before each original API call, owned build descriptors match their pinned baseline and observed class-output membership and hashes remain quiet for at least two seconds. Document-symbol responses are required around that window; this does not establish symbol-model stability or correct Outline rendering. Production guards stay enabled. Intentional build-descriptor negative cases reach the original guard directly.

limitations: Observed Outline conversion and source-model synchronization limitations remain documented. Asynchronous symbols can differ from newer source buffers, and some outside-API range samples remain unresolved; no general Outline fix or warning-free display is claimed. Production snapshot guards remain enabled.

Pure static members, bounded immutable final instance state/field receivers, nested utility packages and proven standard-main UTF-8 text resources, plus existing literal build graphs and supported finite Gradle dependency branches. Mutable state, constructors, external/effectful receivers, arbitrary resources/loaders and build logic remain incomplete.

Source-only hierarchy/overload plus bounded generic substitution, covariance, bounds, erasure and caller result checks; varargs, external/binary/framework and arbitrary dynamic clients remain unverified or refused.

Spring source contracts retain every import/bean/alias in supported exhaustive metadata-dependent selector/registrar branches and literal/annotation/identity processor forms. Arbitrary computed conditions, effects, loops, external contracts and runtime behavior remain unknown or refused.
